title: The ten feet
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The cover is ten feet of seawall, nothing on it, a ruler's exactness. The owner says it's a wall. Wood says it's ten feet. She says of what. He says wall. She says he's not going to tell her and he says no and she says fine and puts it at the front.

panels.composition: The cover: ten feet of concrete seawall, wet, exact, nothing on it.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing a precisely drawn stretch of wet concrete seawall with nothing on it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The laundromat. The LAUNDRY owner. WOOD in the chore coat. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner holding a small booklet and speaking to a young man in a chore coat, black and white, no words

balloons.text: You're not going to tell me.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner in a cardigan, level, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The digest at the front. The ten feet facing the room. Fine. She put it at the front anyway. That's what fine means.

image.prompt: a small booklet placed at the front of a wire rack in a laundromat, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: 'Fine.' At the front anyway. That's what fine means.
